about: Racing's defaults, as data (docs/PLAN-start-a-game-gpt.md track L, L5 part 3b): a sport's standard scoring, lineup slots and locks, and the game specs a sport's Make it a game starts from instead of asking the bot. Stat keys are Racing's (src/lib/sports/racing.ts), one vocabulary for the five series ESPN carries, each series reading what its feed has (F1's sessions, statuses, pit stops and fastest lap; NASCAR's and IndyCar's laps led as laps, bonus and penalty points). The sport's own are NASCAR's (its three series alike); `leagues` has F1's and IndyCar's, which replace them for that series (defaultsFor('racing', 'f1')). A standard game scores a finishing place by a table of places; the game spec's points are one number a stat (A1's schema, on the engine branch), so `points` has the rest and `byPlace` each place stat's table (POS, the race's place in the standings: the disqualified and whoever didn't qualify have none), for when the spec scores places. Places gained (PG) count both ways: a place lost is -1 at 1 a place. The specs are in the game spec's shape; slots and the places aren't in that schema yet (L4 adds them), so they're kept beside it for the spec to read.

scoring.source: DraftKings' NASCAR (its classic contests, as rotowire.com/racing/article/dfs-nascar-101-tips-and-strategies-for-2023-69988, frontstretch.com/2025/02/14/daily-fantasy-nascar-draftkings-forecast-2025-daytona-500 and stokastic.com/articles/dfs-strategy/nascar-dfs-scoring-explained give it; DraftKings' own rules page wasn't readable): the finish 45 for 1st, 42 for 2nd, 41 for 3rd, then a point less a place and two less after the 10th, 20th and 30th (34 for 10th, 32 for 11th, 1 for 40th); a place gained from the start 1 (a place lost -1); a lap led 0.25. Left out: its fastest laps (0.45 each), which ESPN's NASCAR feed doesn't have

categories.source: DraftKings', FanDuel's and F1 Fantasy's racing score points, not categories: none by default

slots.source: DraftKings' NASCAR: six drivers (any six: racing has no positions; its $50,000 salary cap isn't a slot)

season.about: A season of races: draft 6 drivers, all 6 score each race, most points over the season wins.

short.about: One race: everyone drafts a few drivers, every one of them scores, most points wins.

f1.about: F1's own, from the official F1 Fantasy game (2026): its sessions are scored, not only the race.

scoring.source: The official F1 Fantasy game's driver scoring, 2026 (fantasy.formula1.com's rules aren't readable without a browser; as f1pitwall.dev/blog/f1-fantasy-scoring-2026 lists it): qualifying 10 for pole down to 1 for 10th, -5 disqualified; the sprint 8 for 1st down to 1 for 8th, its fastest lap 5, a retirement -10; the race 25, 18, 15, 12, 10, 8, 6, 4, 2, 1 for 1st to 10th, a place gained 1 (a place lost -1), its fastest lap 10, a retirement or disqualification -20. Left out: overtakes (1 each) and driver of the day (10), which ESPN doesn't have, and the constructors' scoring (their own slots: L4)

slots.source: The official F1 Fantasy game: five drivers (its two constructors aren't drivers; its $100M budget isn't a slot)

season.about: A season of races: draft 5 drivers, all 5 score each race weekend, most points over the season wins.

short.about: One race weekend: everyone drafts a few drivers, every one of them scores, most points wins.

irl.about: IndyCar's own: its championship points less its penalties, since its fantasy game publishes no values.

scoring.source: IndyCar's own championship points, one a point (the finish, its qualifying points and its laps-led bonuses, as ESPN gives them), less a penalty's (ESPN's are before them; the season's standings are their sum less the penalties, 2025's and 2026's exactly): the INDYCAR Fantasy Challenge (indycar-fd.ims.com/fantasy/Scoring-Overview) scores the finish, places gained from qualifying, laps led, the best on each team and laps completed, but its values are only in a GridRival league's settings
